scenes.title: The weightless feeling
scenes.text: You tap an app, and it answers instantly. It feels like nothing is there. But the cloud is a place, with walls, with power, and with an address.

scenes.title: A fire in someone else's building
scenes.text: In June twenty twenty-six, a fire broke out at a third-party data center in Dell-ee. Google's servers were not the problem. But a network junction there, called a point of presence, was forced offline by an emergency power shutdown. Google has not said what started the fire.

scenes.title: One junction, three cities
scenes.text: That junction is where traffic enters Google's network. When it went dark, people in Dell-ee, Chen-eye, and Mumbai felt it. Connections slowed down, and some data may have been lost along the way.

scenes.title: The detour has less room
scenes.text: Google rerouted the traffic. But the detours were narrower than the road they replaced. Demand was bigger than capacity, so traffic queued up. And for a while, Google said, there was no workaround.

scenes.title: Weeks to rebuild
scenes.text: Recovery took weeks. Google added capacity, route by route, in Dell-ee, and then in Chen-eye. Crews reached the damaged site on June twenty-second. By June twenty-sixth, service was back to normal.

scenes.title: The cloud has an address
scenes.text: A backup only works if it has room. The cloud is not weightless. It is buildings, power, and cables. And every one of them has an address.
